purpose: Prevent global archipelago screening from inflating frozen-ABM validation by converting every island pollination study into a strict state target.
tier_A_required: an ecological context contrast or externally imposed/natural perturbation that changes pollinator-functional or interaction conditions
a downstream reproductive, floral, demographic or equivalent declared response measured in the same source-defined system chain
classification into the pre-existing frozen state vocabulary without fitting or retuning the ABM to the target
a claim boundary that separates qualitative state compatibility from real-world mechanism identification
tier_A_insufficient_alone: routine pollinator bagging or open-versus-excluded flowers without an external ecological-regime contrast
visitor identity, abundance or richness without a downstream response
single-visit effectiveness without a matched system transition
floral morphology difference without a linked functional or reproductive transition
network architecture without a downstream plant response
colonization frequency or island occupancy without a within-system propagation response
multiple publications connected only by a plausible narrative when their populations, years or estimands are not source-native matched

non_strict_component_examples: Galapagos network summary without a matched reproductive transition
Columbretes residual pollen limitation without a paired pre-loss/two-sided regime
Giannutri network response without a plant reproductive endpoint

claim_boundary: Tier A remains a qualitative external challenge to an already-frozen state class. It does not constitute numerical model fit, causal parameter identification, or evidence that the same ecological mechanism generated matching state labels in different island systems.
